title: Target fractions reduced shared-release sum-noise ratios in seven partial worm map models
abstract: We tested the effect of target strength rules on a shared-release noise model in seven selected C. elegans brain maps. Stored target fractions gave summed-input variance ratios of 1.522 to 1.659 for shared versus independent contact release. Unit contact strengths gave 2.183 to 2.368. Equal total retained strength at each site with equal target shares gave intermediate ratios. Site volume times target fraction gave 1.510 to 1.650. Target input normalization also left lower ratios with fractions. The exact covariance calculation holds release probability fixed and matches means and individual variances within each rule. Positive strengths ensure a sum ratio at least one. These results show amplitude sensitivity, not measured release noise. One adult map lacks target fractions and is excluded. Unknown conductance, release dependence, missing tissue, and no activity fit limit interpretation.

display.caption: Shared-to-independent noise ratios under four strength rules in seven partial worm maps. Lines connect map labels and do not estimate a developmental trajectory.

citations.reason: Reuses the verified panel and tests sensitivity of its unit-strength sum-noise result.
